_what: Downloadable capability kits. A kit is a capability MycOS knows how to use and does not carry until somebody asks for it.
_why: This machine has 54G and sat at 91% full. A tool that costs a gigabyte and runs twice a month is not an installation, it is a rental - so the adapter code lives in this repo (small, ours, edited) and the heavy dependency tree is fetched on install and removed on uninstall.
_the_rule: Disk cost is MEASURED at install and recorded here by the installer, never estimated by hand. A kit that claims a size it was never weighed at is the same false-success shape this project hunts.
_absence_is_a_state: A verb whose kit is not installed reports kit_not_installed with the command that would install it. It does not crash on import and it does not silently degrade - absent and unreachable are different findings (CLAUDE.md).

page_render.title: Rendered page fetch
page_render.what_it_is_for: Official publishers that answer a plain GET with an empty shell. statutes.capitol.texas.gov - the State of Texas publishing its own statutes - is an Angular app that returns 200 and 'Retrieving statute document...'; rendered, the same URL yields 134,919 characters of Chapter 3.

adapted_from.what_we_changed: wrapped as a subprocess that prints JSON, added an official-publisher allowlist, removed every write path - it renders and classifies nothing

_findings.what: torch 2.13.0+cu130 is installed - the CUDA 13.0 build - and torch.cuda.is_available() is False. There is no nvidia-smi and no GPU on this machine.
_findings.cost: nvidia 2.7G + triton 691M + torch 1.2G = 4.6G, of which roughly 3.4G is CUDA runtime that cannot execute here
_findings.remedy: reinstall torch from the CPU index (--index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu), which drops the nvidia and triton trees
_findings.why_not_done: Vision and federated learning both import torch and both are live. A reinstall is a real change to running services and is the principal's call, not a tidy-up to slip into a disk cleanup.
